author: closure-verification workstream (a0/closure/)
purpose: reconcile this workstream's closure verdicts with each runtime workstream's own closure record; name which record is authoritative for which channel and why
authority_rule: A record is authoritative for a channel only if it contains an EXECUTED observation of that channel with a control (unblocked reaches / blocked fails).
A probe that timed out, or that only shows a tool being absent, establishes nothing about closure and must not be reported as closed.
Where two records disagree, the one with the executed two-control observation for the disputed channel wins; the other is retained with its scope narrowed.

lane_e2e_measurements.method: a0/closure/probes/lane_e2e_probe.py -- lane argv built by the runtime's OWN code, executed for real; the model is asked to run the shared canary through its shell tool and to PERSIST the canary's stdout to a file, so the model's prose is never the evidence

results.canary: LANE_PROBE dns=fail:gaierror tcp=fail tcpvia=none https=fail:URLError local=ok egress=BLOCKED

results.posture: closed (its shipped CliSolver argv: codex exec --sandbox workspace-write)
results.canary: LANE_PROBE dns=fail:gaierror tcp=fail tcpvia=none https=fail:URLError local=ok egress=BLOCKED

agreements: their channel_detail.codex_lane.note states the same fact as this workstream's F2: KAPSO DOES expose a lane-level codex sandbox parameter (agent_specific.sandbox, codex_agent.py:117) whose default is danger-full-access, and the claude lane has no equivalent parameter
their recipe.not_closed_by and this workstream agree that the codex lane's default is what plan:569 describes
the barrier observations agree: unshare-rn blocks egress and the registered evaluation still scores identically under the barrier

contradictions.their_evidence: lane_probes.codex_workspace_write = {returncode: 124, timed_out: true, command_ran: false, egress_ok: false} -- the probe TIMED OUT and the in-lane command never ran
contradictions.this_workstream: closed, measured: returncode 0, model call completed, in-lane canary persisted egress=BLOCKED (evidence/11_kapso_lane_closed.json)
contradictions.why: a timed-out probe and a probe that never ran its command cannot support a closure claim; the executed run here does, and it also shows the model call still completes (rc=0), which is the part that matters for A0/A1 usability
contradictions.effect: their verdict is UPGRADED from inference to evidence; the channel is genuinely closable by ONE config key (agent_specific.sandbox=workspace-write), not only by a code change

contradictions.their_evidence: lane_probes.claude_with_tool_bans: command_ran=false, network_reached=false; the agent's own reply 'the Bash tool isn't available in this session'; lane_closure_by = ['claude lane: agent_specific.disallowed_tools removes Bash']
contradictions.their_claim: the claude lane is closed by config
contradictions.this_workstream: NOT closed as a runtime lane; closure here is achieved by DELETING the shell tool
contradictions.authoritative: this workstream for the study-level verdict; theirs for the narrow statement 'with Bash banned, this lane cannot run shell commands'
contradictions.why: removing Bash closes the network by removing the capability the coding lane exists to use, and (a) their probe therefore observed an ABSENT tool, never a DENIED network attempt, and (b) a KAPSO coding lane without Bash cannot run the registered evaluation through its own machinery, which is the premise A0.1 rests on. This is the same defect class as `claude --restricted`
contradictions.effect: claude lane verdict must read CONDITIONAL (external cut or lane switch), not closed

contradictions.issue: lane_backend_evidence still says 'No model call was attempted in this probe, so the lane stays UNPROBED', while lane_probes.codex_reachable / claude_reachable are model calls; and unprobed_channels is [] although the codex closed-posture probe timed out
contradictions.effect: documentation defect in that record; no measurement conflict with this workstream

agreements: complete agreement with this workstream's F1: the shipped full-run driver is codex_exec, it carries no sandbox parameter, its argv bypasses the sandbox, and it enables live web search; closure is possible ONLY by switching the driver to codex_tmux with web_search disabled
both records show the codex_tmux/workspace-write posture blocked (their curl exit 7; this workstream's canary dns/tcp/https fail with local=ok)
both records show the unsandboxed/shipped posture open (their HTTP 200; this workstream's egress=OPEN)

contradictions.detail: their verdict 'egress_detected' describes EvE AS SHIPPED; this workstream's closure.eve.json 'closed' describes the codex_tmux posture the protocol recipe names, with the shipped path recorded as a separate OPEN mechanism
contradictions.authoritative: theirs for 'EvE as shipped'; this workstream's for the per-mechanism/posture breakdown
contradictions.why: neither claim is wrong, they answer different questions; the study must quote both together (EvE = CONDITIONAL, shipped default OPEN)

contradictions.channel: evidence that the model lane is reachable
contradictions.detail: their observed.agent_lane.cmd finished with rc=124 (40s timeout) yet the conclusion reads 'the agent lane is reachable: codex completes a model call'
contradictions.authoritative: this workstream (evidence/07_model_lane_blocked.log rc=0 'OK'; evidence/08, 09, 11, 11b, 13, 13b all rc=0)
contradictions.why: rc=124 is a timeout kill and does not support a reachability claim; the claim is nevertheless true and now has clean executed support

contradictions.detail: their record notes the shipped driver pins model gpt-5.6-sol while the provider answered as gpt-5.6-terra
contradictions.action: relay to the EvE workstream: a full EvE run must confirm the configured model id is served before A0.1/A0.2 numbers are trusted

agreements: external isolation is the mechanism, not configuration

docker --internal keeps siblings reachable while killing egress (their sibling_postgres/sibling_redis ok), and it also cuts the host route (their host_loopback_127_0_0_1_5432 fail; this workstream's 02_host_loopback_cut.log)

contradictions.their_evidence: their own caveats say 'the probed lane is the evaluator/candidate lane, which is the only lane this adapter can drive' and that the codex backend 'could not be exercised'
contradictions.this_workstream: the LLM lane was measured by this workstream: the codex backend selects `--sandbox workspace-write`, and that exact CLI posture is now proven closed with the model call completing (evidence/08, 13). The DEFAULT backend (kilocode, `kilo run --auto`, no closure switch) is still OPEN by construction and cannot even start here (`kilo` not installed)
contradictions.authoritative: theirs for the candidate/evaluator channel; this workstream's closure.loreley.json for the LLM lane and for the default-backend verdict
contradictions.why: their caveat about the unusable model lane was true when written and is now obsolete; their verdict does not cover the channel the protocol's closure requirement is about (autonomous acquisition by the agent lane)
contradictions.effect: Loreley stays CONDITIONAL: codex backend closed, default kilocode backend open/unprobeable, evaluated lane closed under external isolation

agreements: no contradiction: their record explicitly states 'The solver lane is NOT covered by this verdict in isolation: with --solver codex|claude the substrate inherits that CLI's network posture. A closed deployment must run the solver lane inside the same barrier (probe with --probe-cmd) or use --solver injected.'
both records treat the injected lane as closed under unshare -rn, and both use the two-control pattern

resolution.channel: CLI solver lane (now implemented: a0/runtimes/simpleloop/a0_adapter/solvers.py, CliSolver._command -> codex exec --sandbox workspace-write)
resolution.why: it is the executed end-to-end measurement of that lane with a model turn and a persisted in-lane canary; the SimpleLoop record explicitly leaves this channel open
resolution.effect: SimpleLoop's study verdict moves from CONDITIONAL/inconclusive to CLOSED for its shipped solver argv; re-probe if the solver CLI changes

cross_runtime_consequence: All four substrates can now run under the SAME access policy on this host: codex workspace-write with web search disabled (KAPSO by one agent_specific key, SimpleLoop by its shipped argv, EvE by driver switch, Loreley by backend switch). That is what plan:591-603 requires of the A1 comparison.
EvE's shipped default remains the outlier: any EvE arm must state which driver it ran, because codex_exec (open) and codex_tmux (closed) are not the same experiment.
